records.region: Southern central Labrador, the southern lake-fed approach to lower Goose River and inner Goose Bay/Lake Melville beside Happy Valley-Goose Bay.
records.material_pending_reason: The westernmost selected opening and initial southeastward feeder cross a small-pond and wetland/upland strip. The acquired imagery exposes local water and parts of the drainage corridor but does not independently establish the complete narrow through-link into the first large selected lake. This is a geographic source gap, not simply an unnamed tributary or a requirement for exact banks.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The west-to-east selection follows a southern lake-and-stream route while a broader river occupies a separate northern valley. The southern stream visibly joins that northern river before the selected lower meanders. The route then passes the road bridge north of the airport/town and reaches the sandy delta at the inner bay. The farther-south broad river corridor is outside the selection.
records.completion_scope: All 22 selected parts were considered. The lake/outlet/confluence corridor and actual lower river mouth are supported, while the complete initial feeder-to-lake connection remains a material source gap.
records.supported_name_scope: The lower receiving river has independent Goose River usage. No name is transferred to all upstream ponds, lakes or the southern tributary.

scope_limits: The westernmost selected feeder-to-first-lake through-link remains insufficiently established. This is the sole primary material-pending reason.
No local lake names or tributary name is assigned. Peters River/Lindo Lake is a regional lead only; an unlocated label is not selected-route evidence.
Goose River is a lower receiving identity; the full119.972km rendered object is not asserted to bear one uniform river name.
The inspected imagery establishes no required reservoir or managed transfer along the selected corridor. Absence of visible controls is not an operational history or an exhaustive dam inventory.
Historical publication failures, ordinary image limitations and the remaining route gap are kept distinct. No exact-bank, present-discharge, official-length or registry conclusion is made.

records.region: East Greenland, south of the Geikie Plateau label, extending through the glaciated coastal-rock belt to a historical ice-front/coastal-water transition.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The permitted national original continuously covers the selected glaciated and exposed-rock terrain through the historical ice-front/coastal-water ending, but establishes no representative named natural river. A regional plateau label cannot name this whole modeled object.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The single mainstem fragment opens in glaciated terrain among exposed-rock projections, turns northeast and east, bends southeast, continues east through a rock-bounded ice passage and then turns south to the coastal ending. There are no supplied tributary fragments.
records.completion_scope: Every selected part and join was read against the continuously covering original, including the complete final part and actual endpoint. No meaningful unseen geographic interval remains. Geographic completion does not require exact banks, present-day glacier position or proof of a natural river beneath the ice.

scope_limits: Natural-river identity and surface/subglacial hydraulic continuity remain unestablished.

publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
